x: Article 27, like Articles 25 and 28, is available to all persons; Article 26 is available to religious denominations or any section of them.

s: To whom does Article 26 guarantee the freedom to manage religious affairs?
x: Article 26 is a right of religious denominations or sections, unlike Articles 25, 27 and 28 which are available to all persons.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Fundamental Rights provisions?
o: Article 21A provides the Right to Education
Article 24 prohibits employment of children in factories
Article 27 provides freedom to manage religious affairs
Article 26 provides freedom to manage religious affairs
x: Freedom to manage religious affairs is Article 26; Article 27 concerns taxes for promoting religion.

s:
Assertion (A): The Right to Freedom of Religion comprises four Articles.
Reason (R): The Right to Freedom of Religion is covered by Articles 25 to 28.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
x: The Right to Freedom of Religion has four Articles because it spans Articles 25 to 28, so R explains A.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct?
o: Article 26 – A religious denomination's right to manage its religious affairs
Article 27 – No compulsory tax for promotion of a particular religion
Article 28(1) – No religious instruction in institutions wholly maintained out of State funds
Article 28(3) – Attendance at religious instruction can be made compulsory in State-aided institutions
x: Article 28(3) protects freedom from compulsory attendance: no person can be compelled to attend religious instruction without consent.

s: The Supreme Court has left it to the Ministry of Education to decide whether schools imparting religious instruction fall under which provision?
x: The question left to the Ministry of Education is whether such schools fall under Article 26(a), rather than under Articles 19(1)(g) or 30(1).

s: To what are the rights of religious denominations under Article 26 subject?
o: Security of the State and public order
x: Article 26 lets a denomination set up institutions and own and administer property, all expressly subject to public order, morality and health.

s: Under Article 28(3), what is the position of attendance at religious instruction in a State-recognised or State-aided institution?
o: Compulsory only for students of that religion
Voluntary, with a guardian's consent needed for a minor
x: Article 28(3) makes attendance voluntary; no one can be compelled, and a minor needs the guardian's consent.

s: What does Article 27 prohibit?
o: Any fee for the secular administration of religious institutions
Compelling payment of taxes whose proceeds promote a particular religion
Use of taxes to support all religions equally
x: Article 27 bars taxes for promoting a particular religion; it does not bar fees, and taxes may support all religions equally.

s:
Consider the following statements about Articles 27 and 28:
1. Article 27 bars taxes, but not fees, for promoting a particular religion.
2. Article 28(1) bans religious instruction in institutions wholly maintained out of State funds.
3. Article 28(1) applies to State-administered institutions set up under a trust requiring such instruction.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; by Article 28(2), clause (1) does not apply to institutions set up under an endowment or trust requiring instruction.

s: Unlike Article 25, to which of the following are the rights under Article 26 NOT subject?
x: Article 26 is subject to public order, morality and health, but not to 'other provisions of Part III' as Article 25 is.

s: Which provisions are regarded as state-neutrality provisions in matters of religion?
x: Article 27 (no tax for one religion) and Article 28(1) (no instruction in wholly State-funded institutions) keep the State neutral.

s: Which Article of the Constitution says that no person shall be compelled to pay any taxes whose proceeds are used to promote or maintain any particular religion?
x: Article 27 bars compelling anyone to pay taxes whose proceeds promote a particular religion.

s: 'No religious instruction shall be provided in any educational institution wholly maintained out of State funds.' Which provision of the Constitution says this?
x: Article 28(1) bars religious instruction in institutions wholly maintained out of State funds; 28(3) makes it voluntary in aided or recognised institutions.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Church of God — Loudspeakers are subject to public order
Ratilal — State cannot touch essential religious practices
Stanislaus — Propagation does not include a right to convert
St. Stephen's — State may completely abolish minority-institution autonomy
x: St. Stephen's is associated with minority-institution autonomy; it did not hold that the State may completely abolish such autonomy.

s: In which year did the Supreme Court formulate the Essential Religious Practice test?
x: The ERP test was formulated in 1954 to identify practices integral to a religion; the Constitution does not define 'essential'.

s: With which case is the Essential Religious Practice doctrine associated?
x: Shirur Mutt is associated with the ERP doctrine; Stanislaus concerned conversion, Bijoe Emmanuel the National Anthem and Shayara Bano instant triple talaq.

s: In the Sabarimala judgment (2018), what was the exclusion of women of a certain age group held to be?
o: Protected because Ayyappa devotees are a separate denomination
x: The 4:1 majority of the five-judge Bench held the exclusion was not an ERP and that Ayyappa devotees were not a separate denomination.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about State anti-conversion laws?
o: The Orissa Act, 1967 and the MP Act, 1968 arose from concern over missionary activity
Later amendments widened their scope to conversions to Islam
Stanislaus held that propagation does not include forcible conversion
In Stanislaus v. State of MP (1977), the Supreme Court struck down these laws
x: Stanislaus upheld these laws, holding that the right to propagate does not include forcible conversion.

s: In which case was Section 295A IPC upheld on public-order grounds?
o: Ramji Lal Modi v. State of UP
Rev. Stanislaus v. State of MP
x: Section 295A was upheld in Ramji Lal Modi; Stanislaus dealt with anti-conversion laws.

s: In 2022, what did the Karnataka High Court hold about wearing the hijab?
o: Identical to carrying a kirpan under Article 25
x: The Karnataka High Court held in 2022 that hijab was not an Essential Religious Practice; the Allahabad High Court relied on this in August 2026.

s: What did the Supreme Court hold about polygamy in Javed (2003)?
o: Not an essential religious practice protected by Article 25
A practice protected only for religious denominations
An essential religious practice absolutely protected by Article 25
A secular activity regulated exclusively under Article 23
x: In Javed (2003), polygamy was held not to be an essential religious practice protected by Article 25.

s: Who headed the nine-judge Bench that heard the 2026 Sabarimala review reference on the Essential Religious Practice doctrine?
x: A nine-judge Bench headed by CJI Surya Kant heard the reference; the Centre argued the burden lies on the person challenging a practice.

s: In which case did the Supreme Court declare instant triple talaq invalid?
x: Shayara Bano (2017) invalidated instant triple talaq, leaving polygamy and nikah halala open.

s: By which Bench and majority was the Sabarimala judgment of 28 September 2018 delivered?
x: Sabarimala (2018) was a 5-judge, 4:1 decision; the 2026 review is before a 9-judge Bench.

s: In the Sabarimala case (2018), what did the Supreme Court hold about Ayyappa devotees?
o: Are not a separate religious denomination
Are covered by Explanation II to Article 25
x: The Court held Ayyappa devotees are not a separate denomination and the age bar on women is not an ERP.

s: Who were the first women of the barred age group to enter the Sabarimala temple, in January 2019?
x: In January 2019, Bindu Ammini and Kanaka Durga became the first women of the barred age group to enter Sabarimala after the 2018 verdict.

s: Section 295A of the IPC, upheld in Ramji Lal Modi v. State of UP, now corresponds to which section of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita?
x: Section 295A IPC (upheld on public-order grounds in Ramji Lal Modi) is now Section 299 BNS.

s: What is the maximum punishment for sacrilege under Punjab's Jaagat Jot Sri Guru Granth Sahib Satkar (Amendment) Act?
x: The Act, which got assent in April 2026, provides for punishment up to life imprisonment; it is challenged in the Punjab and Haryana High Court.

s: In which year was the Orissa Freedom of Religion Act, an early State anti-conversion law, enacted?
x: The Orissa Act is of 1967 and the MP Act of 1968; both were upheld in Stanislaus (1977).

s: Which case upheld the Orissa and Madhya Pradesh anti-conversion Acts?
o: Rev. Stanislaus v. State of MP
Ramji Lal Modi v. State of UP
x: Rev. Stanislaus (1977) held that propagation does not include conversion and upheld both Acts.

s: What does Karma refer to in Hinduism?
o: The law of action and consequence
x: Karma is the law of action and result; Dharma is duty, Samsara the cycle of rebirth and Moksha liberation.

s: What does the Tripitaka refer to in Buddhism?
x: The Tripitaka is the Buddhist sacred texts; the Sangha is the monastic order, the Dhamma the Buddha's teachings and Nirvana liberation.

s: What does Sallekhana refer to in Jainism?
x: Sallekhana is the Jain ritual fast unto death; Kaivalya is liberation, a Tirthankara a spiritual teacher and Ahimsa non-violence.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: The Khalsa is the Sikh brotherhood; the Guru Granth Sahib is the holy book, the langar the community kitchen and the Dasam Granth another Sikh text.

s: What is the Ashrama of the householder called in Hinduism?
x: Grihastha is the householder stage; Vanaprastha is the forest-dweller stage.

s: What does Ahura Mazda refer to in Zoroastrianism?
o: The highest grade of fire temple
x: Ahura Mazda is the supreme god of good, while Angra Mainyu is the destructive or evil spirit.

s: What is the Atash Behram in Zoroastrianism?
o: The highest grade of fire temple
x: Atash Behram is the highest grade of fire temple; the Zend Avesta is the holy book, Angra Mainyu the evil spirit and Ahura Mazda the supreme god.

s: What does Angra Mainyu (Ahriman) refer to in Zoroastrianism?
x: Angra Mainyu is the evil spirit; Ahura Mazda is the supreme god of good.

s: What does the term Tirthankara mean in Jainism?
x: Tirthankara means 'Ford-maker'; there are 24, from Rishabhanatha to Mahavira.

s: Who compiled the Adi Granth, which became the Guru Granth Sahib?
x: Guru Arjan compiled the Adi Granth; the Guru Granth Sahib is the holy book and eternal Guru of the Sikhs.

s: What does Aparigraha refer to in Jainism?
x: Aparigraha is non-possession, one of the five vows; Sallekhana is the fast unto death and Kaivalya liberation.

s: What is Shahenshahi (Shenshai)?
o: Calendar used mainly by Indian Parsis
x: Shahenshahi (Shenshai) is a Parsi calendar, along with Kadmi and Fasli.

s: What is the Dakhma (Tower of Silence) among the Parsis?
o: The calendar used by Indian Parsis
A raised structure where the dead are exposed to vultures
x: The Dakhma is where the dead are exposed to vultures; the Atash Behram is the highest-grade fire temple.

s: What is the holy book of the Zoroastrians (Parsis)?
x: The Zend Avesta is the holy book of Zoroastrianism; the Tripitaka is Buddhist and the Adi Granth Sikh.

s: Who was the first Tirthankara of Jainism?
x: Of the 24 Tirthankaras, Rishabhanatha was the first and Mahavira the last.

s: Who among the following was the 24th and last Tirthankara?
x: Mahavira was the 24th and last Tirthankara; Rishabhanatha was the first.

s: What does Kaivalya refer to in Jainism?
x: Kaivalya is liberation in Jainism; Aparigraha is non-possession, Sallekhana a fast unto death, Tirthankara a ford-maker.

s: What is an Agiary among the Parsis?
x: An Agiary is a Zoroastrian fire temple; the Atash Behram is the highest grade of fire temple.

s: Who among the following regarded religion as a form of collective worship of society and examined the distinction between the sacred and the profane?
x: Emile Durkheim associated religion with collective worship of society and distinguished the sacred from the profane.

s: In July 2026, which community renewed its demand for a separate religion code in the Census?
x: The Ravidassias renewed their demand for a separate religion code in the Census in July 2026. Jains, Parsis and Buddhists are already counted as separate religions in the Census, and all three are among the six notified minorities, so they have no such demand.

s: Which thinker linked karma, dharma and caste with the shaping of economic life in *The Religion of India*?
x: Max Weber examined the relationship of karma, dharma and caste to economic life in *The Religion of India*.

s: Which period does the Bhakti movement, which rejected ritualism and caste, roughly span?
x: Bhakti spans the 6th to the 18th century, and its interaction with Sufi traditions built communal harmony and regional literatures.

s: Which of the following hinders religious pluralism?
o: Freedom to practise any religion or none
x: Religious pluralism is the freedom and security to practise any religion or none, resting on freedom of religion and mutual respect; exclusivism hinders it.

s: The Arya Samaj's call 'Back to the Vedas', seeking to restore a golden past, is an example of what?
x: Revivalism seeks to restore a golden past, as in 'Back to the Vedas'; fundamentalism is a return to literal scripture rejecting plural readings.

s: Which mutt is the hereditary Dharmakarta of the Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams (TTD)?
x: The Sri Swamy Hathiramji Mutt at Tirupati is the hereditary Dharmakarta of the TTD; the AP Endowments Act, 1987 regulates Hindu temples and mutts.

s: Communalism, separatism and fanaticism are identified in India as forms of what?
x: Communalism, separatism and fanaticism are the forms of religious fundamentalism identified in India.

s: To whom did Bammera Potana offer his Andhra Maha Bhagavatamu?
x: Bammera Potana offered his Andhra Maha Bhagavatamu to Lord Rama, not to King Krishnadevaraya.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Asghar Ali Engineer — Writings on communalism
T.N. Madan — Critique of the Western secularisation thesis
x: *Homo Hierarchicus* and the analysis of caste through purity-pollution are associated with Louis Dumont, not B. Malinowski.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: J.G. Frazer — Religion as the opium of the people
Karl Marx — Magic, religion and science
x: E.B. Tylor associated the origin of religion with animism, or belief in spirits. Marx is associated with the opium formulation, Frazer with magic-religion-science, and Weber with the Protestant Ethic.

s: According to Census 2011, what was the share of Hindus in India's population?
x: Hindus were 79.8% in 2011, below 80% for the first time.

s: According to Census 2011, which is India's largest religious minority, at 14.2%?
x: Muslims form 14.2%; Christians 2.3%, Sikhs 1.7% and Buddhists 0.7%.

s: In The Golden Bough, J.G. Frazer traced which sequence?
x: Frazer's The Golden Bough traces human thought from magic to religion to science.

s: Who among the following held that strong personal attachments and death are the source of religion?
x: Malinowski traced religion to strong personal attachments and death; Tylor linked it to animism and Durkheim to the sacred and the profane.

s: Which Andhra Pradesh law regulates temples and mutts in the State?
x: The AP Endowments Act, 1987 regulates temples and mutts in Andhra Pradesh.

s: According to Census 2011, which religious group formed 2.3% of India's population?
x: Census 2011: Christians 2.3%, Sikhs 1.7%, Buddhists 0.7%, Jains 0.4%.

s: How many religious communities are notified as minorities by the Centre?
x: Six communities are notified minorities: Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists, Parsis and Jains.

s: Under which Article did the 44th Amendment, 1978 place the Right to Property?
x: The 44th Amendment deleted Articles 19(1)(f) and 31 from Part III and made property a constitutional legal right under Article 300A.

s: After the 44th Amendment, 1978, how many Fundamental Rights does the Constitution contain?
x: The Constitution originally had seven Fundamental Rights; the 44th Amendment deleted the right to property (Articles 19(1)(f) and 31), leaving six.

s: In which Part of the Constitution is Article 300A, on the right to property, placed?
x: The 44th Amendment (1978) moved the right to property to Article 300A in Part XII, Chapter IV, making it a legal right.

s: What does Article 300A provide?
o: No citizen shall be deprived of property except by executive order
No company shall be deprived of property under any circumstances
No person shall be deprived of property except with the consent of Parliament
No person shall be deprived of property save by authority of law
x: Article 300A states that no person shall be deprived of his property save by authority of law.

s: What did the Andhra Pradesh High Court emphasise in GGR Housing v. State?
o: Strict statutory due process in land acquisition under Article 300A
The abolition of Article 300A as a legal right
The conversion of the right to property into a Fundamental Right
The exclusion of land acquisition from judicial review
x: The Andhra Pradesh High Court insisted on strict statutory due process in land acquisition under Article 300A. Article 300A protects the right to property as a legal constitutional right.

s: Through which remedy is the right to property under Article 300A enforced?
x: Article 300A is not a Fundamental Right, so it is enforced through Article 226 or a suit, not Article 32.

s: To whom is the right to property under Article 300A available?
o: All persons, including non-citizens and companies
Citizens and non-citizens, but not companies

s: What does Article 30(1A), inserted by the 44th Amendment, mainly deal with?
o: Exemption of minority institutions from all State regulation
Compulsory acquisition of property of minority educational institutions
Appointment of teachers in minority institutions
Reservation of seats in minority institutions
x: Article 30(1A) concerns compulsory acquisition of the property of a minority educational institution. The amount fixed must not restrict or abrogate the right guaranteed by Article 30.

s: To whom does Article 30(1) give the right to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice?
x: Article 30(1) covers all minorities, religious or linguistic; the State may regulate standards but may not take away their minority character.

s: Under Article 29(1), who has the right to conserve a distinct language, script or culture?
x: Article 29(1) protects any section of citizens with a distinct language, script or culture; it is not limited to minorities.

s: How is Article 30(1) described?

s: Which Article directs every State to provide instruction in the mother tongue at the primary stage to children of linguistic minority groups?
x: Article 350A directs every State and local authority to provide mother-tongue instruction at the primary stage for linguistic minority children.

s: Under Article 30(1), to whom does the right to establish and administer educational institutions belong?

Although voting is a statutory right, which of the following have been recognised under Article 19(1)(a)?
1. Right to know the details of candidates
2. NOTA option
3. Secrecy of the ballot
x: Candidate details, NOTA and ballot secrecy have all been recognised under Article 19(1)(a), though voting itself is statutory (the 'voting paradox').

s: What is the status of the Right to Work under Article 41?
x: Article 41 is a Directive Principle, not a Fundamental Right; the right to information, by contrast, is read into Article 19(1)(a).

s: Which case held that voting is only a statutory or legal right?
o: Kuldip Nayar v. Union of India (2009)
x: Kuldip Nayar (2009) held that voting is only a statutory/legal right, not a Fundamental Right.

s: Which Article provides for adult suffrage at 18 years?
x: Article 326 provides adult suffrage at 18; the right to vote itself is statutory under the RPA.

s: Under which section of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 is the right to vote provided?
x: The right to vote is a statutory right under Section 62 of the RPA, 1951.

s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Linguistic minorities – one of the six notified religious categories
x: The six notified religious minorities are Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists, Parsis and Jains; linguistic minorities are not among them.

s: What is the unit for determining a linguistic minority in India?
x: The State is the unit for determining a linguistic minority; numerical inferiority and non-dominant status are relevant, and the Constitution does not define the term.

s: How is the term 'minority' treated in the Constitution of India?
x: The Constitution uses 'minority' in Articles 29, 30, 350A and 350B without defining it; the NCM Act, 1992 also does not define it.

s: What kind of body is the National Commission for Minorities?
o: Statutory body under the NCM Act, 1992
x: The NCM is statutory, set up under the NCM Act, 1992 - not a constitutional body.

s: In March 2026, Kerala's Malayalam Bhasha Bill was contested as harming which linguistic minority in Kasaragod?
x: The Malayalam Bhasha Bill was contested as harming the Kannada linguistic minority in Kasaragod.

s: The LARR Act, 2013 replaced the Land Acquisition Act of which year?
x: The LARR Act, 2013 replaced the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 and made Social Impact Assessment mandatory.

s: Under the LARR Act, 2013, compensation in rural areas can go up to how many times the market value?
x: LARR compensation is up to 4x market value in rural areas and 2x in urban areas.

s: Under the LARR Act, 2013, after how many years is unused acquired land returned?
x: Under the LARR Act, 2013, land not used within five years is returned.

s: Which of the following is compulsory under the LARR Act, 2013?
x: The LARR Act, 2013 makes Social Impact Assessment compulsory.

s: Under the LARR Act, 2013, compensation in urban areas can go up to how many times the market value?
x: Compensation can go up to 2 times the market value in urban areas and 4 times in rural areas.

s: Which Amendment provided that land under personal cultivation could be acquired only on paying market value?
x: The 17th Amendment required market value for land under personal cultivation; Article 31 itself was deleted by the 44th Amendment, 1978.

s: Which Amendment inserted Article 31C, saving laws that give effect to Articles 39(b) and 39(c)?
x: Article 31C came with the 25th Amendment (1971); Articles 31A and 31B came with the 1st (1951).

s: Article 31B protects Acts placed in which Schedule from challenge on Fundamental Rights grounds?
x: Article 31B (1st Amendment, 1951) shields Acts in the Ninth Schedule.

s: In I.R. Coelho (2007), Ninth Schedule laws inserted after which date were held open to basic structure review?
x: I.R. Coelho (9 judges) held laws added to the Ninth Schedule after 24 April 1973 open to basic structure review.

s: In which case was the 42nd Amendment's extension of Article 31C to all Directive Principles struck down?
x: Minerva Mills (1980) struck down the 42nd Amendment's extension of Article 31C to all DPSPs.

s: Which Article saves laws providing for the acquisition of estates from challenge on Fundamental Rights grounds?
x: Article 31A, inserted by the 1st Amendment (1951), saves laws on acquisition of estates; 31B protects Ninth Schedule Acts.

x: St. Xavier's College (Ahmedabad), 1974, a nine-judge bench, limited State control over minority college management.
